title: THE n-FOOTING DISCRIMINATOR: deep-end data vs n = 2.000 (DE a0) / n = 1.660 (RAR a0)

mapping.one_function: g_obs = g_N mu(g_N/a0), mu(x) ~ x^(n-1) deep -> d log g_obs/d log g_N -> n
mapping.task_relation: deep slope -> n/2; the deep end reads n = 2*beta
mapping.seesaw: n = Lambda^2/(a0 M_Pl) = s_Lambda/a0, s_Lambda = 2 a0_DE
mapping.family_note: mu_n(u) = 1-(1+u)^(-n): deep mu ~ n*u linear for every n; deep RAR slope = 1/2 identically; n is the amplitude (a0 = s/n). Slope channel = form test; amplitude channel = the seesaw itself.

MIGHTEE.source: G099 register, digitized Fig.3 (0.036 dex rms), 90% below 0.2 a0_DE

SPARC.source: G071 register, 641 rings / 35 isolated low-EFE galaxies

HI.registered_7_tail: 7/26 LT at V_max-based g_N < 0.1 a0 (G114), median r -0.094 dex (context only)
HI.source: G114 register, LITTLE THINGS single points; g_bar = G M_b/R^2

n_amp_pooled_between_sample.note: deep samples mutually inconsistent (MIGHTEE 0.98 / SPARC-deep 2.92 / HI 1.29)

superluminality_kill.bound: minimal Pade family: n <= 2 (H046 G1); n = 2 saturates; n > 2.01 kills

wedge.statement: the deep end wants the LARGER a0 (1.2-1.9e-10, n ~ 1.0-1.66) AND the mode count wants n = 2.000 (a0 = 9.36e-11): jointly inconsistent if n(a0) = s/a0 runs -- at the deep end's own scale the seesaw gives n ~ 1.0 (2.000 excluded by the +0.15 dex deep offset, 5.1 sigma-log)

verdicts.V1: measured deep exponents: SLOPE channel n = 2*beta: MIGHTEE 0.89+-0.09 pooled / 1.20+-0.11 per-gal; SPARC 0.93+-0.05 pooled / 1.19+-0.10 per-gal; HI 1.33+-0.43; pooled 1.24+-0.04 per-galaxy reading (0.93+-0.05 ring). AMPLITUDE channel n = s/a0_eff: MIGHTEE 0.98, SPARC-deep 1.35, HI 1.29, pooled 1.28.
verdicts.V2: separation: slope channel n = 1.24+-0.04: vs 2.000 20.3 sigma, vs 1.660 11.2 sigma (per-galaxy pooled); ring-level n = 0.93+-0.05: vs 2.000 22.0 sigma, vs 1.660 15.0 sigma. Amplitude: MIGHTEE n = 0.98+-0.11: vs 2.000 9 sigma, vs 1.660 6 sigma.
verdicts.V3: V3 THE HONEST STATEMENT -- does today's deep data adjudicate the footings?  YES, against the DE-anchored n = 2.000, and against n = 1.660 in the slope channel; the wedge sharpens into a real tension at ~5 sigma.  THE NUMBERS.  (1) The deep RAR slope over g_N < 0.2 a0 measures beta = 0.622 +- 0.019 per-galaxy (ring-pooled 0.466 +- 0.024, flattened by galaxy-mixing): the asymptotic form is the quadratic 1/2, whose window-exponent is n = 2*beta = 1.24 +- 0.04; the seesaw footings predict beta = n/2 = 1.000 (n = 2.000) and 0.830 (n = 1.660) -- excluded at 20.3 sigma and 11.2 sigma (per-galaxy pooled) respectively.  (2) The deep-end AMPLITUDE (the seesaw itself, n = s/a0_eff): MIGHTEE n = 0.98 +- 0.11 (a0 = 1.90e-10); SPARC deep rings n = 1.35 +- 0.19 (a0 = 1.38e-10 -- the sub-DE end of the deep rings); HI dwarfs n = 1.29 +- 0.45 (a0 = 1.45e-10).  The deep-end samples are mutually inconsistent on the amplitude (MIGHTEE +1.9x vs DE, SPARC-deep -1.5x) but NONE sits at n = 2.000: the DE footing is excluded by every deep-end reading at >= 3 sigma, and MIGHTEE -- the largest deep sample -- excludes even n = 1.660 at 6 sigma.  (3) THE WEDGE: the deep end wants the LARGER a0 (1.2-1.9e-10, RAR-class) AND the full-curve mode count wants n = 2.000 at a0 = 9.3619e-11; with n(a0) = s/a0 running, the pair is jointly inconsistent: at the deep end's own preferred scale a0 = 1.843e-10 the seesaw gives n = 1.016, i.e. the n = 2.000 claim fails by the deep-end offset (MIGHTEE +0.15 dex deep, 5.1 sigma-log, G133; the offset closes only at the MIGHTEE scale where n ~ 1.0).  The ALT footing n = 1.660 is the deep end's SPARC-consistent value and its amplitude is the closest deep-end reading to the data, but the deep SLOPE still excludes its n/2 = 0.830 at ~11.2 sigma (the slope is the quadratic 1/2).  KILL CHECK: the measured n sits 20.6 sigma BELOW the n = 2.01 superluminal kill line -- no kill, the deep end is nowhere near n > 2 by 1pct; the danger is instead the OPPOSITE one: every deep-end channel reads n <= 1.7, i.e. the observed n does NOT saturate the subluminality bound at the deep end (the saturation claim rests on the full-curve L232 rms separation of 0.016 dex, not on the deep end).
